'''Gary Clark Jr.''' (born November 16, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Yokohama B-Corsairs]] of the [[Japan]]ese [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] where he was named the [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|American Athletic Conference Player of the Year]] for the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]]. He made his [[NBA]] debut in 2018 and played in four straight seasons across multiple teams, including the [[Houston Rockets]], [[Orlando Magic]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and [[New Orleans Pelicans]].

==High school career==
Clark was born in [[Smithfield, North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gobearcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/gary-clark/7097|title=Gary Clark|work=gobearcats.com|access-date=January 29, 2024}}</ref> He played basketball at [[Clayton High School (North Carolina)|Clayton High School]] in [[Clayton, North Carolina]], where he left as the school's all-time leading scorer, rebounder and shot-blocker. He is also the only North Carolina high school player to record a quadruple-double.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Potter|first1=Mike|title=Freshman and Clayton native Gary Clark is already turning heads at Cincinnati|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article10115711.html|access-date=March 9, 2018|work=[[The News & Observer]]|date=November 3, 2014}}</ref> Clark was ranked as the No. 100 overall prospect by ESPN, No. 87 by Rivals and No. 90 by 247sports. He committed to [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] on September 18, 2013, after receiving a scholarship offer from [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].<ref name="newsrecord">{{cite news|last1=Szelest|first1=Jason|title=Gary Clark: The problem that will never be forgotten|url=http://www.newsrecord.org/sports/gary-clark-the-problem-that-will-never-be-forgotten/article_cb46eee0-2d02-11e8-8043-63558dd83422.html|access-date=May 3, 2018|work=The News Record|date=March 21, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Clark made an immediate impact for Cincinnati, entering the starting lineup from day one and becoming the first freshman to start a season opener for the program since [[Lance Stephenson]]. At the close of the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) season, he was named to the league's all-rookie team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Abner|first1=Josh|title=Clayton native Gary Clark's way is the Cincinnati Bearcat way|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/community/smithfield-herald/sh-sports/article16201754.html|access-date=March 9, 2018|work=[[The News & Observer]]|date=March 24, 2015}}</ref> Clark posted 7.8 points, 7.2 rebounds, 1.0 steal and 1.3 blocks per game as a freshman.<ref name="newsrecord"/>

In his sophomore season, Clark developed into one of the top defensive players in the AAC. After averaging 10.4 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 1.5 blocks per game, he was named second-team All-AAC and the conference Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rauch|first1=Jeremy|title=UC's Gary Clark named AAC Defensive Player of the Year|url=http://raycomgroup.worldnow.com/story/31427766/ucs-gary-clark-named-aac-defensive-player-of-the-year|access-date=March 9, 2018|work=[[Raycom Media]]|date=March 6, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Prior to his junior year, Clark was named to the preseason All-AAC first team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Groeschen|first1=Tom|title=UC's Caupain named AAC preseason Co-Player of Year |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2016/10/24/ucs-caupain-named-aac-preseason-co-player-year/92677398/|access-date=March 9, 2018|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> He averaged 10.8 points and 7.9 rebounds per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nguyen|first1=Thuc|title=UCLA basketball: 5 games to watch|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2017/11/07/ucla-basketball-5-games-to-watch/|access-date=May 3, 2018|work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]|date=November 7, 2017|archive-date=May 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504092638/https://www.pe.com/2017/11/07/ucla-basketball-5-games-to-watch/|url-status=live}}</ref>

At the close of his senior season, Clark was named AAC Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year. He averaged 12.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks per game. Clark led Cincinnati to an AAC regular season title.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Groeschen|first1=Tom|title=UC Bearcats' Gary Clark named AAC basketball Player of the Year|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2018/03/07/ucs-gary-clark-named-aac-player-year/402848002/|access-date=March 9, 2018|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=March 7, 2018}}</ref> He was the AAC tournament Most Outstanding Player after averaging 16.3 points and 11.7 rebounds in the conference tournament. Clark hit a game-winning free throw with four seconds in regulation to secure a 56–55 victory for the Bearcats in the title game.<ref name="newsrecord"/>

==Professional career==
===Houston Rockets (2018–2020)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Clark signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]] on July 5, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rockets sign rookies Gary Clark and Vincent Edwards and waive Aaron Jackson |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=21629 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 5, 2018}}</ref><ref name=standard>{{cite news|title=Rockets Announce Roster Updates|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-updates|date=December 6, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 6, 2018}}</ref> On December 6, 2018, his contract was converted to a standard NBA contract.<ref name="standard" /> During the 2018–19 season, he appeared in 51 regular season games and two playoff games for the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gary Clark 2018-19 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/clarkga01/gamelog/2019|website=basketball-reference.com|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref> He also played 10 games with the Rockets' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref name=realgm>{{cite web|title=Gary Clark|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Gary-Clark/Summary/79987|website=realgm.com|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref>

After playing for the Rockets in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]], Clark re-joined the team for the 2019–20 season.<ref name="realgm" /> In November 2019, he had three stints in the G League with the Vipers.<ref name="realgm" /> On January 7, 2020, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Waive Gary Clark|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-gary-clark|date=January 7, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2020–2021)===
On January 14, 2020, Clark signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Gary Clark to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-gary-clark-10-day-contract-20200114|date=January 14, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 14, 2020}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract on January 29,<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Gary Clark to Second 10-Day Contract|url= https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-gary-clark-second-ten-day-20200129|date=January 29, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 29, 2020}}</ref> and a rest-of-season contract on February 8.<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Gary Clark for Remainder of Season|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-gary-clark-remainder-season-20200208|date=February 8, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref>

On November 23, 2020, Clark re-signed with the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Re-Sign Gary Clark|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-resign-gary-clark-nba-free-agency-20201123|date=November 23, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 23, 2020}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Clark and [[Aaron Gordon]] were traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Gary Harris]], [[R. J. Hampton]], and a future first round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-gordon-and-clark-20210325|title=Denver Nuggets acquire Aaron Gordon and Gary Clark from Orlando Magic|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> On April 9, he was waived after making two appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nugs-sign-shaquille-harrison-20210409|title=Denver Nuggets sign guard Shaquille Harrison to two-way contract|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2021|access-date=April 9, 2021}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2021)===
On May 11, 2021, Clark signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-gary-clark-two-way-contract|title=76ers Sign Gary Clark to Two-Way Contract|date=May 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=May 11, 2021}}</ref> He made two appearances for the 76ers, recording averages of 1.0 rebounds, 0.5 assists, and 0.5 steals.

===Mexico City Capitanes (2021)===
In November 2021, Clark joined the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mexico City Capitanes announce opening night roster for 2021–22 season|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/news/mexico-city-capitanes-announce-opening-night-roster-for-2021-22-season/|website=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2021|access-date=November 6, 2021}}</ref> In eight games to start the [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–22 season]], he averaged 14.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 1.1 assists in 31.3 minutes per contest.<ref name="Pels2021">{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Gary Clark|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-gary-clark|website=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2021|access-date=December 3, 2021}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2021–2022)===
On December 3, 2021, Clark signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], becoming the first Capitanes' player ever to receive an NBA call-up.<ref name="Pels2021" /> On January 7, 2022, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans waive Gary Clark|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-gary-clark|access-date=January 7, 2022|date=January 7, 2022|website=NBA.com}}</ref> Two days later, he re-signed with the Pelicans on a two-way contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans sign Gary Clark to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-gary-clark-to-two-way-deal|access-date=January 9, 2022|date=January 9, 2022|website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Return to Mexico City (2022–2023)===
In November 2022, Clark re-joined the Mexico City Capitanes for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/roster|title=Capitanes de Ciudad de México roster 2022-23|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Illawarra Hawks (2023–2024)===
On June 24, 2023, Clark signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] in Australia for the [[2023–24 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/hawks-swoop-on-import-forward-gary-clark|title=Hawks Swoop on Import Forward Gary Clark|work=Hawks.com.au|date=June 24, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref>

===Yokohama B-Corsairs (2024–present)===
On June 13, 2024, Clark was selected by the [[Valley Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA G League expansion draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-25 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2024-expansion-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2024|access-date=June 14, 2024}}</ref> On August 6, he signed with the  [[Yokohama B-Corsairs]] of the [[Japan]]ese [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gary Clark ex Illawarra joins B Corsairs |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/885818/Gary-Clark-ex-Illawarra-joins-B-Corsairs |website=Asiabasket |access-date=August 7, 2024 |date=August 6, 2024}}</ref>
